chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of al-asan ibn Ali al-Washa, on the authority of Ahmad ibn A'ez, on the authority of Abi Khadijeh, on the authority of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The people go forth upon three types: a scholar, a seeker of knowledge, and scum (the rest). We are the scholars, and our followers are the seekers of knowledge, and the rest of the people are scum.

key_terms.غَثَاءٌ: Scum / The remainder / The general public

ai.seo_question: What are the three categories of people according to Imam al-Sadiq in this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) to establish a theological hierarchy where scholars (*al-‘ulama’*) and their devoted followers (*al-muta’allimūn*) form the core of the community, while the rest are termed *ghutha’* (scum or dregs). This classification underscores the Shia emphasis on the transmission of knowledge (*naql*) as the primary criterion for spiritual and social standing, distinguishing the knowledgeable elite from the general populace who lack religious insight.
